title: ReasoningReport
description: C3.3. The one object that is the frontend's props, the download artifact, the cached blob and the golden-test subject. FROZEN AT G1 (end of W4). After the freeze: additive changes only -- a new field must be optional. A breaking change requires bumping `schema_version`, regenerating the three fixtures, and a note to the frontend owner in the same PR. `additionalProperties: false` is set at every level on purpose: it is what makes the freeze mechanical rather than a promise, because adding a field then requires editing this file, which is visible in review.

schema_version.description: Bumped only by a breaking change. A reader that understands 1.0 may assume every required field below is present.

arms.description: One entry per strategy attempted. A failed arm is PRESENT with status `failed`, never omitted -- an absent arm is indistinguishable from an arm that was never run, and B6.5 requires the other arms to render while saying plainly that this one did not.

is_trap.description: ADR-005 withdrew the trap floor: 0 of 16 candidates reproduced over 120 runs, and every bank item now carries `false`. The field stays because it is a real property of an item and M2 may yet earn one -- but it is a DECLARATION until a reproduction log backs it.

versions.description: Everything needed to reproduce this report, and the cache key's inputs. C2.3/I3: a published number is reproducible or it is not published.

prompts.description: PROMPT_BUNDLE_VERSION -- a content hash over prompts/*.md, so it cannot drift from the prompts it names.

model_pin.description: The GENERATION pin's fingerprint. ADR-001 redefined this from a dated id to a tuple (model, file digest, quantization, runtime, temperature, top_p, seed, reasoning effort) because an id does not reproduce a local number.

model_pin_fields.description: The pin tuple spelled out, so a report is self-describing without the reader holding ADR-001 open. Optional: the fingerprint is the identity; this is the courtesy.

judge_triage_pin.description: MODEL_ANALYZE -- the exact dated id that produced the behavior and validity rows.

judge_escalate_pin.description: MODEL_ESCALATE. Null until M2-5 builds the escalation tier; a report with escalated steps and a null pin here is not publishable.

analyzer_backend.description: ADR-001 makes local-only a measured configuration, not a fallback. Which one produced these labels is part of the provenance, because the calibration harness scores both and they do not have to agree.

status.description: `failed` means the provider call did not return after its retry (C4.1). DISTINCT from `degraded`, which means the arm ran and one downstream stage did not: a failed arm has no trace to show, a degraded one has a trace it cannot fully annotate.

trace_quality.description: C3.1. `provider_summarised` is not a flavour of `partial`: the text is real but second-hand, and a reader must be told which. `partial` also covers a trace with reasoning and NO visible answer -- M1-8 found one (mb-08.thinking looped 126 times and never answered), and calling that `full` makes the downstream `correct: false` assert the model answered and was wrong.

correct.description: Null when the answer could not be parsed, which is a THIRD outcome and not a quiet `false`. M1-5 paid for this distinction: `unparsed` means we could not read it, `false` means the model was wrong, and collapsing them slanders the model.

escalation_capped.description: C4.4: ESCALATION_MAX_STEPS bound, so some flagged steps carry only the cheap verdict. The cap is auditable precisely because this is in the report rather than in a log.

budget_bound.description: C4.1. Locally this is a MEASUREMENT that the trace reached the nominated budget rather than evidence the provider truncated it -- ollama exposes reasoning effort, not a token cap. A bound budget silently caps the very metric B4 #7 measures, which is why it renders.

step_id.description: C3.2's `{strategy}:{span_id}:{ordinal}`. THE JOIN KEY FOR EVERY LABEL EVER WRITTEN. The ordinal comes from the segmenter, frozen as `segmenter-frozen-v1`; changing the segmenter renumbers these and silently detaches every human label from its text (Hazard 1).

behavior.description: Null on a degraded arm -- an unannotated step, which is the honest rendering when the classifier could not produce a conforming row. NEVER a default label: the whole point of C4.3's parse-failure rule is that a fabricated `linear` is worse than a blank.

label.description: Gandhi et al. (arXiv:2503.01307 A3). Single-label with the precedence backtracking > verification > backward_chaining > subgoal_setting > linear, stated verbatim in both the prompt and calibration/rubric.md.

error_type.description: Names the defect in an `unsound` step, and is null otherwise. Per-type recall is the reportable thing (Appendix B): a judge that catches arithmetic and misses dropped constraints is a specific, useful finding that an aggregate hides.

escalated.description: The frontier tier re-judged this step and its verdict REPLACED the triage verdict (C4.4). Always false in Month 1; M2-5 builds the tier. It renders, so a reviewer can see which flags were double-checked.

consistency.description: C4.5. Asks ONLY: given these numbered steps, does the final answer follow? Not whether the answer is right in the world -- that is `correct`, and conflating them would let a right answer with broken reasoning pass. Null until M2-8 builds the checker.

then.description: A4.3's rule, enforced here rather than trusted: a `contradicts` verdict that cites nothing is an accusation with no evidence, and it is the shape a hallucinating judge produces.

reasoning_tokens.description: Counted locally with the model's own encoding, not reported by the runtime (S1, G0 check 2). Null when the encoding for that model is unknown -- a guessed count is plausible and wrong, and every cost figure downstream would inherit it.

pattern_profile.description: Share of classified steps per behavior class. Sums to ~1 over an arm with labels; absent on a degraded arm rather than all-zeros, because zeros would read as 'we looked and found none'.

classifier_repairs.description: Chunks that needed C4.3's repair retry and then succeeded. In the report rather than a log because a rising repair rate is the leading indicator of the parse-failure rate M1-9's DoD caps.

degraded.description: The arm ran; a downstream stage did not complete. Null is the normal case. Every reason here is a state FE-8 must be able to render in mock mode -- a state reachable in production but not in a fixture becomes a Month-3 conversation in the month with no slack for them.

scoreboard.description: B4 #7's headline, per item. ADR-006 narrowed what this may claim: the arms do NOT separate on accuracy on this bank (0 of 16 items), so the defensible contrasts are COST (1.2-13.3x for the same answer) and TOOLS (arm 3 turned 3 wrongs into rights). `accuracy_delta_pp` stays in the schema and is usually 0 -- a measured zero is a finding, and deleting the field would hide it.

measurement_context.description: I3: every score renders next to its own error bars. Month 1 cannot populate any of this -- the calibration run is M2-17 -- so every field is nullable, and a null renders as 'not yet measured' rather than as a good number. A UI that silently omits this block when null defeats the invariant.

majority_class_baseline.description: C5.5. A kappa reported without this is unreadable: `linear` is the dominant class, so a high raw agreement can mean the rubric is easy rather than the classifier good.
